newsitem.title: USA: Mercury to start auto lending in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Mercury to start auto lending in Canada.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co plans to expand its consumer auto lending business into Canada in early 1997, chairman, president and chief executive John Brincat said on Wednesday at a Piper Jaffray investment conference.
Brincat said the company will open a Toronto office in January. He said it will be the company's first office outside the U.S..

James Doyle, senior vice president and controller of Mercury Finance, said in an interview that he is comfortable with the First Call consensus earnings estimates of $0.81 per share in 1996, $0.98 per share in 1997 and $1.21 per share in 1998.

Brincat told the conference that the company is in talks with a group covering 90,000 physicians on a plan to offer consumer financing for elective surgeries including male hair transplants, "tuck jobs" and other "enhancements to the anatomy." He said it has the potential to be a "very lucrative" business for Mercury Finance.

Brincat said in an interview that the plan to finance elective surgeries requires that people who choose that payment method would have the physician's office forward an application to Mercury which would review the applicant's credit history and then make a decision on whether to extend credit.
It could become 10 percnet of our total portfolio," Brincat said.
He said the average elective procedure costs about $3,100.
Brincat also told the conference that Mercury Finance is in talks with a large "captive" lender about a program in which Mercury would take on the financing activity in the used car area.
He did not identify the other company in his remarks and during an interview he declined to be more specific.
